concepts.title: Meristematic and Permanent Tissues
concepts.definition: Plant tissues are grouped into meristematic tissues of actively dividing cells at apical, intercalary and lateral positions, and permanent tissues, which are simple tissues like parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma, and complex tissues like xylem and phloem.
concepts.key_idea: Xylem conducts water with tracheids, vessels, fibres and parenchyma, while phloem translocates food through sieve tubes, companion cells and phloem fibres.

solution_steps.explain: Decide whether the tissue is meristematic or permanent.

concepts.title: Monocot and Dicot Root, Stem and Leaf Anatomy
concepts.section: 6.3 Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants
concepts.definition: Internal anatomy distinguishes dicot and monocot organs: dicot roots show xylem and phloem in separate radial bundles with exarch xylem, monocot stems have scattered vascular bundles with no cambium, and dicot leaves show reticulate venation with mesophyll split into palisade and spongy parenchyma.
concepts.key_idea: Ground tissue system, vascular tissue system and epidermal tissue system together build the internal structure of root, stem and leaf in both groups.

solution_steps.explain: Note ring versus scattered bundles, and radial versus conjoint types.

concepts.title: Secondary Growth: Cambium, Annual Rings, Heartwood and Sapwood
concepts.definition: In dicot stems and roots secondary growth arises from the vascular cambium and cork cambium, which form secondary xylem, secondary phloem, and periderm; activity differences form spring wood and autumn wood or annual rings, and the darker inner wood becomes heartwood while the outer functional wood is sapwood.
concepts.key_idea: Cork cambium produces phellem and phelloderm making up periderm, which replaces the epidermis of the older stem and protects it.

solution_steps.explain: Identify vascular cambium and cork cambium in the section.
Trace secondary xylem, secondary phloem, phellem and phelloderm.
